messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Proposal: multi-year prepay, ramp bridging & payment terms (Orion Health)

Samir —

Thanks again for the deep dive yesterday. Attached is a straightforward commercial outline to convert our pilot into a production commitment while addressing the ramp volatility you raised. High-level ask from your side was: protect cashflow during year 1 ramp, get a predictable unit price, and avoid a multi-year vendor lock without testing periods.

Proposal summary (attached: Orion_SOW_v3.pdf, redwood_pricing_matrix_v5.xlsx):
- 3-year term, annual prepay by invoice year (Year 1, Year 2, Year 3).
- Acceleration / ramp bridging: Redwood provides a 6-month escrow-backed bridge for the incremental capacity shortfall in Y1 (escrow holdback released on milestone completion).
- Payment split option A: 40% upfront prepay Year 1, 30% at 6-month milestone, 30% at 12-month true-up (we can invoice milestone payments Net 60).
- Standard discount schedule: 18% off list for 3-year full-annual prepay vs 10–12% for 2-year. We can create a blended ramp credit if you prefer a stepped discount tied to usage bands.

Key open items for procurement:
1) Net terms on milestone invoices (you requested Net 90 for some customers)
2) Escrow governances and release criteria
3) Early termination or portability for regulated workloads

If this looks directionally right I’ll loop in Finance (Laura) and RevOps (Dylan) to draft the invoice flow and escrow language.

Next steps: confirm which payment split you want (A above, or a 30/30/40 variant), and whether Net 90 is required for the milestone invoices or just the final true-up.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Orion_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf, 8 pages)
Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v5.xlsx (xlsx, 1 sheet)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karla Soto <ksoto@orionhealth.com>, procurement@orionhealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: multi-year prepay, ramp bridging & payment terms (Orion Health)

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few constraints from procurement/finance side:
- Our standard is Net 90 for vendor invoices tied to enterprise contracts. We can accept Net 60 for the final true-up only if we get a 50% escrow or some commercial credit to offset cash timing.
- For Year 1, we cannot prepay more than 35% of the ARR as a single upfront due to internal budget windows.
- We need ramp protection: if usage in months 4–6 is >150% of forecast, we will pay for the overage on Net 90 but want a short-term capacity guarantee.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood reduce Year 1 upfront to 30–35% and spread the remainder across two milestone invoices?
2) If we push to Net 90 on the milestone invoices, can you provide a contingent credit schedule (ramp credit) that returns up to 15% of the prepay if usage is under 50% at the 12-month true-up?

If we can agree on those points, I’ll escalate to Karla (CFO) for signature.

Samir
Sr. Director, Cloud Procurement
Orion Health

Team —

Heads-up: Orion is pushing for Net 90 on milestone invoices and wants Year 1 upfront capped at 35%. They also asked for a contingent ramp credit that refunds some of the prepay if usage is low at true-up.

Can Finance/legal weigh in on: escrow structure, acceptable holdback %, and whether we can operationalize a 12-month contingent credit? From Commercial: what discount movement do we need if we accept Net 90 on milestones?

Suggested internal approach:
- Offer: 30% upfront prepay (Y1) + two milestone invoices (25% at 6 mo, 45% at 12 mo true-up) with Net 60 payment for milestone invoices by default; concede Net 90 for milestone invoices only if Orion accepts a 50% escrow of the upfront and an annual true-up cap.
- Discount: keep 3-year list at 18% but reserve an additional 2–3% concession if they demand Net 90 across the board.

Thoughts?
Jonas

Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: multi-year prepay, ramp bridging & payment terms (Orion Health)

Jonas —

Finance comments:
- Escrow: acceptable operationally. We need clear release triggers: (a) 6-month usage >= 80% of forecast -> release 50% of escrow; (b) 12-month true-up -> remaining escrow released or returned pro rata. Escrow agent recommended: independent custodian (we can provide a template).
- Holdback %: 50% of Year 1 upfront is high. Recommend 25–35% holdback tied to 6-month milestone.
- Net terms: we can accept Net 90 on milestone invoices only if escrow is in place and Orion commits to a minimum annual consumption floor (a guaranteed minimum spend for Y1).
- Contingent ramp credit: operationally doable but must be formulaic (e.g., if Y1 usage < 50% of forecast at 12-month true-up -> return 10–15% of upfront). We need precise bands to avoid disputes.

I will draft a short attachment (prepay_terms_draft.docx) with defined bands and escrow triggers. If Legal signs off, we can offer: 30% upfront, 25% at 6m, 45% true-up; 30% escrow holdback; Net 90 allowed on milestone invoices conditioned on escrow. The discount for the 3-year prepay stands at 18% but we can offer an additional 2% if Orion accepts the 30% escrow and an irrevocable minimum spend commitment.

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: prepay_terms_draft.docx (docx, 2 pages)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: commercial compromise for Orion Health

All —

Commercial compromise I recommend to keep the deal moving:
- Offer: 30% upfront (Y1) + 30% at 6 months + 40% at 12-month true-up.
- Escrow: 30% holdback on the upfront only; release 50% at 6 months if usage >= 75% of forecast, full release at 12-month true-up.
- Net terms: milestone invoices default Net 60; we will allow Net 90 on the 6-mo milestone only if Orion accepts a 1.5% additional discount on Year 1 billed amounts (to offset financing). Net 90 on the final true-up is not acceptable without a stronger minimum spend guarantee.
- Ramp credit: formulaic refund up to 12% of upfront based on bands (0–50% usage -> 12% refund; 50–75% -> 6% refund; >75% -> no refund).

This keeps cash protected, addresses Orion's timing constraints, and limits our downside on extended Net 90. Happy to present this as a single redline to SOW and Terms & Conditions.

Ben Carter
VP, Global Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
